description.short_caption: Chest radiograph showing bilateral pulmonary infiltrates after clinical deterioration.
description.detailed_description: This is an anteroposterior chest radiograph showing diffuse bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, predominantly in the mid and lower lung zones. The heart and mediastinum appear enlarged, and there are visible medical devices, including bilateral shoulder prostheses and indwelling lines. The lung fields demonstrate a hazy appearance consistent with interstitial or alveolar involvement, which may suggest infection, edema, or other pathology.

description.short_caption: Axial chest CT showing pulmonary abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT image demonstrates a cavitary lesion in the upper lobe of the right lung, with surrounding consolidation and possible air-fluid level. The left lung appears relatively clear. The mediastinum and bony structures are visible, with no obvious abnormalities in these regions. The image is presented in a soft tissue window.
visible_findings: cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe
surrounding consolidation in the right lung
possible air-fluid level in the cavity

description.short_caption: Chest CT scan showing bilateral pulmonary abnormalities.
description.detailed_description: This axial chest CT scan reveals bilateral pulmonary abnormalities, including areas of consolidation and ground-glass opacities, predominantly in the lower lung fields. The mediastinum and heart are centrally located, and there is no obvious pleural effusion. The scan is presented in a lung window setting, highlighting parenchymal changes.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of bone marrow showing a granuloma (200x).
description.detailed_description: This is a high-power (200x) histopathology image of bone marrow stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E). The image shows a well-formed granuloma, characterized by a central area of necrosis surrounded by a ring of epithelioid histiocytes and lymphocytes. The arrow points to the granuloma, while the arrowhead indicates adjacent marrow elements. The cellular composition and organization are consistent with a granulomatous inflammatory response.

description.short_caption: H&E stain of bone marrow showing granulomas and cellular changes.
description.detailed_description: This is a histopathology image of bone marrow stained with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) at 80x magnification. The image shows multiple granulomas (indicated by arrows) with central necrosis surrounded by inflammatory cells. The background reveals a mix of hematopoietic cells and areas of marrow fat. The granulomas suggest a possible infectious or inflammatory process.
